alex: Hey team — we're getting a bunch of timeouts on long generations (20-30s). Using the Python SDK v0.6.2. Example exception: `httpx.ReadTimeout: CancelledReadError(read timeout)` even though I set `timeout=30` on the client. Anyone seen this?

nina: Can you paste the client init + the exact arg you set? Also the trace/logs if available.

alex: here's the minimal repro I used:
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout=30)
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1", prompt="long", max_tokens=1500)
print(resp.text)
```
Stack: `httpx._exceptions.ReadTimeout: ReadTimeout(10.000000)`
I also tried `export REDWOOD_CLIENT_TIMEOUT=30` and restarting, no change.

sam: quick thought — in many libs `timeout` is split into connect/read/write. Are you sure the SDK maps that single `timeout` to read timeout? Could be connect-only.

kai: FYI there was a behavior in v0.6.2 where streaming/read timeouts fell back to a 10s default. Non-streaming should honor the global `timeout`, but streaming code path used a hardcoded read timeout. infra-bot deployed a patch today to address it.

infra-bot: Deployed: python-sdk v0.6.3 -> fixes: respect global timeout for non-streaming long generations; added explicit `stream_read_timeout`/`stream_connect_timeout` config. Release notes: https://internal/release/py-sdk/v0.6.3 :rocket:

maya: try upgrading to 0.6.3 and set `timeout=40`. If you're using `stream=True`, also set `stream_read_timeout=60`.

nina: if possible include `REDWOOD_DEBUG_HTTP=1` logs (httpx debug) and the SDK `request_id` from the error payload. That helps correlate with runtime logs.

alex: upgraded to 0.6.3. Non-streaming calls are now fine. But when I switch to `stream=True` to reduce latency, I'm still hitting a `StreamReadTimeout(10s)` after ~10s on long gens. Example: `client.generate(..., stream=True)` -> yields a chunk or two, then timeout.

sam: streaming tends to keep the connection open and the SDK will read frames; the SDK exposes separate stream timeouts. Try:
```py
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout=40, stream_connect_timeout=10, stream_read_timeout=120)
for chunk in client.generate(..., stream=True):
    process(chunk)
```
That explicitly raises the read window for streams.

kai: also confirm you aren't using a reverse proxy with shorter idle timeout (nginx, alb). Some customers saw 15s timeouts at the LB layer that looked like SDK timeouts. Check the `X-Request-Id` across logs.

nina: if after setting `stream_read_timeout` explicitly you still see 10s, please capture SDK debug logs and the `request_id` and post here; we'll escalate to eng-runtime with the trace.

alex: doing that now. Repro steps I'm running locally: small loop that calls `client.generate(stream=True, prompt=long_prompt)`, Python 3.10, httpx 0.24.3. Request id: `req_01H9Y8ABCD`. Logs attached (trimmed) show `StreamReadTimeout after 10.0s`.

infra-bot: Created support ticket #SUP-3482 and paged eng-runtime with request_id `req_01H9Y8ABCD` :bell:

maya: thanks — looks like two things: (1) upgrade if you haven't; (2) try explicit `stream_read_timeout` and confirm proxy timeouts. If both fail we'll ask eng-runtime to check kernel/thread scheduling or the serving-side keepalive.

alex: got it, will try explicit param and test via curl + chunked responses to isolate SDK vs infra. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
